from itertools import product

n = 23
fixed = {5:-1, 10:-1, 13:1, 19:1}
c_fixed = {12:0, 13:-3, 16:0, 19:-1}

def compute_c(s, k):
    return sum(s[i]*s[i+k] for i in range(n-k))

# Try with random restarts / backtracking

# Backtrack assigning positions, pruning with sum of squares and fixed c constraints
# c_k depends on all pairs at distance k. c_19 has only 4 terms (i=0..3), c_16 has 7 terms, c_13 has 10, c_12 has 11.

# Let's do DFS with pruning. At each step s[0..p-1] assigned. For k where n-k <= p, c_k is fully determined.
# For k=19: determined when p>=20 (pairs i=0..3, i+19=19..22, so need p>=23... wait)
# c_k uses s[0..n-k-1] and s[k..n-1]. Fully determined when all indices < p. So when p >= n, i.e., p=23.

free_idx = [i for i in range(n) if i not in fixed]
print(len(free_idx))  # 19

import itertools
count = 0
solutions = []
for bits in itertools.product([-1,1], repeat=len(free_idx)):
    s = [0]*n
    for i,v in fixed.items(): s[i]=v
    for idx,v in zip(free_idx, bits): s[idx]=v
    # check c constraints

            ok=False; break
    if not ok: continue
    total = sum(compute_c(s,k)**2 for k in range(1,n))
    if total <= 59:
        solutions.append((total, s))
        if total <= 59:
            print(total, s)
            break
    count+=1
print("done", len(solutions))
